{"model":"pam","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are observing a person's daily activities to build a procedural memory of when\nand how a household robot should help them.\n\n# Environment\n- The setting is a home with a dining table, a kitchen sink and a dishwasher, where a single person lives.\n- The designated storage area: the kitchen sink, where used cups, bottles and bowls are put. Drinks such as water and cola are kept in the fridge.\n\n# Proactive Assistance Goals\n- bringing the person an object they may need next.\n- putting away objects the person appears to have finished using.\n- operating home appliances the person habitually operates by hand, such as turning on the living-room air conditioner when they sit down to watch TV.\n- etc. –- any helpful action that is grounded in observed behavior.\n\n# Inputs\n- Current memory: the (trigger, action) entries that were applied today\n- Today's observations: a time-stamped log of the person's activities made by an object detector and a vision-language model from the robot's camera\n- Summary: what the person and robot each did in today's observations, in temporal order\n- Human feedback: today's feedback from the person, may be absent\n# Task\n- Given the current memory, today's observations, the summary, and human feedback, update\nthe memory of (trigger, action) rules.\n- The memory will be used by the robot to proactively assist the person in future\ndays, so the goal is to produce a memory that helps the person as much as possible.\n\n# Update Instructions\n- Use the observations, summary, action history, current memory, and human feedback to\nupdate the memory rules.\n- First, explicitly RE-STATE the pick-and-place actions that the human performed in\nthese observations and summary. Then, for EACH of those human actions, think concretely\nabout HOW the robot could have taken that action over on the person's behalf (e.g.,\nby bringing the object to the person earlier, or putting it away afterwards). Your\nrules should be built around these take-over opportunities –- do NOT invent rules\nfor objects or actions the human did not interact with in these observations and summary.\n- Each rule's action MUST literally mirror an action the human performed in these\nobservations and summary: the picked-up object, the destination, and the object→\ndestination motion must all correspond to something the human actually did. Do NOT\ninvent hypothetical actions.\n- If a trigger describes the person already in motion with an object (e.g., \"reaches\n for X\", \"picks up X\", \"pours X\"), the object the person is in motion with MUST be\nDIFFERENT from the object the rule's action manipulates. Same-object triggers are\nforbidden.\n- Deployment caveat: when this memory is deployed, the human will act expecting the\nrobot to help. So any rule whose trigger is phrased as \"person picks up X\", \"person\nfetches X\", or \"person moves X\" risks never firing –- the robot would have picked X\nup first, leaving no human action to observe. Each rule's trigger must describe an\nobservable cue the human will produce REGARDLESS of robot assistance.\n- Default to ADDING a new rule whenever the summary mentions a human pick-and-place\naction that the robot could plausibly take over and that is not yet covered by the\ncurrent memory. It is better to add a rule that may need refinement later than to\nomit a useful take-over opportunity. Err on the side of MORE rules, not fewer.\n- Refine an existing rule when its trigger or action is too rigid, too loose,\nambiguous, or otherwise misaligned with helpful robot behavior.\n- IF AND ONLY IF a memory rule's action is in the memory AND the summary shows the\nhuman (not the robot) performed that action: this is most likely NOT because the\naction is unnecessary, but because the rule's trigger was too strict, so the robot\ndid not fire –- and consequently the person ended up doing it themselves. For ONLY\nthat specific rule, extend its trigger by appending an additional observable cue\nwith `or` (e.g., `<original cue> or <a cue that occurs earlier or is more visually\ndistinct>`). Keep the original cue intact and just append. Do NOT modify the\ntriggers of any other rules –- only the rule whose action was performed by the human\n.\n- Remove a rule only when it is clearly wrong, such as when the trigger fired but\nthe action would have been inappropriate.\n- Before finalizing the updated memory, mentally re-apply it to TODAY'S video as if\nyou were the inference module: walk through each video moment and ask \"would this\ntrigger fire when intended? would it mis-fire when it shouldn't?\" If a rule would\nmis-fire or fail to fire at its intended moment, revise its trigger (or remove the\nrule) before producing the final output. Use the thinking trace to make this\nverification pass explicit.\n- Do not remove a rule simply because its trigger did not occur in today's observations.\n- If human feedback is provided, treat it as authoritative and prioritize it over\nyour own judgment.\n\n# Output explanations\n- trigger: a single short natural-language statement describing the visible event/\nmoment that should cause this rule's action to fire. The trigger MUST be self-\ncontained.\n- action: exactly one of these task names, copied character for character: 컵 치우기, 사용자에게 물어보기, 세탁물 건조기로 옮기기, 에어컨 켜기, 컵에 물 채워 주기, 컵에 콜라 따라 주기, 라면 끓이기 알려 주기, 전자레인지로 데우기 알려 주기, 부름에 응하기, 물 한 잔 가져다주기, 맥주 가져다주기, 맥주 캔 치우기. Write state descriptions and triggers in Korean.\n- Coaching tasks (라면 끓이기 알려 주기, 전자레인지로 데우기 알려 주기) fire only when the person asks how to do it or says they are stuck. Never add, move, rewrite or remove rules for them.\n# Output (JSON only, no markdown, no commentary)\n{\n  \"rules\": [\n    {\"trigger\": \"<NL statement>\", \"action\": \"<string>\"},\n    ...\n  ]\n}\n"},{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Today's observations, provided as a chronological time-stamped log:\n07:58:02 사람 보임\n08:10:40 사람이 말함: 「컵 치워 줘」"},{"type":"text","text":"Current memory:\n{\n  \"rules\": [\n    {\n      \"trigger\": \"사용자가 컵을 식탁 등에 두고 자리를 비웠고, 아무도 컵을 들거나 만지지 않는다.\",\n      \"action\": \"컵 치우기\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n\nSummary:\n08:10:40 컵 치우기 부탁\n\nHuman feedback:\n다 마신 뒤에만 치워 줘"}]}],"temperature":0.3,"max_tokens":16384,"stream":false,"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true}}
